source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Use Ireasoning MIB browser professional:
1. Enable SNMP v3 agent settings from WEB UI. (Refer to WebGUI spec/user guide).
2. Enable the corresponding user account SNMPv3 settings at WEB UI.
3. Open Ireasoning MIB browser, load the MIB files.
4. Setup the settings of MIB browser to access BMC according to the WEB UI SNMPv3 settings.
5. Left-click on the $target and expand subtree.
6. Right-Click on the node and use "Get Next" or "Get Subtree" to get all the values of the $target.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
Use NetSNMP to check.
1. Enable SNMP v3 agent settings from WEB UI. (Refer to WebGUI spec/user guide).
2. Enable the corresponding user account SNMPv3 settings at WEB UI.
3. Put the mib files into the netsnmp search path.
http://www.net-snmp.org/docs/FAQ.html#Where_should_I_put_my_MIB_files_
4. Use NetSNMP "get type" of command(s) to retrieve the values of the $target from BMC.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- SNMP_configureSP.spClock monitors/configures the SP clock via SNMP; agent reads the OID with curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" -k https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/DateTime 2>&1 (Redfish DateTime) as an alternative, but the SNMP-configured SP-clock path needs the BMC SNMP agent + a 2nd host to walk the spClock MIB.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return FULL Redfish DateTime JSON (as the SP clock source) so the user can cross-check the SNMP spClock value; the SNMP walk of the spClock OID needs the configured agent + 2nd host.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: agent reads Redfish DateTime as SP-clock evidence; the actual SNMP spClock set requires operator SNMP config + care (time changes affect logs).

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL; calls the case monitor/configure, substitutes a TLS-bypassed credential-bearing Redfish GET for SNMP and never resolves whether a clock SET is required.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: BLOCKED / CHANGED; correctly identifies the irreducible read-versus-write conflict and clock/log/certificate impact.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 760/2291 remains PARTIAL while repeating the unsafe Redfish shortcut without resolving operation semantics.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Its BLOCKED result is non-counting history; the substantive decision is independently confirmed, while its skipped row-762 next key is corrected from the XLSX and manifest.

original_test_intent: Validate the service-processor clock through SNMP, but the preserved source does not establish whether the required function is read-only clock accuracy/visibility or a state-changing `spClock` configuration and readback test.
original_method: Items say `configureSP.spClock`, while Procedure and Criteria only use IReasoning/Net-SNMP Get Next/Get Subtree on undefined `$target`; no SNMP SET, value, reference, readback or restore action is defined.
manual_activity: Engineering must first decide whether this case is a read-only SNMP clock comparison or a writable clock configuration test. An engineer then configures SNMPv3; any SET additionally requires explicit approval, maintenance ownership and observed restore/recovery.
required_inputs: authoritative GET-only versus SNMP SET test purpose
vendor `spClock` numeric OID, ASN.1 type, read/write access and encoding
UTC/local/timezone/DST semantics, synchronized reference and allowed delta
SNMPv3 auth/privacy profile and manager ACL
Redfish endpoint discovery, CA validation and documented cross-interface equivalence if used
if SET: approved test value/offset, NTP interaction, maintenance window, affected logs/certificates/scheduled tasks and exact restore method
safety_requirements: Do not issue SNMP SET, Redfish PATCH or any time change until engineering resolves the operation and explicitly approves value, impact and restore.
Do not run DeepSeek's `curl -k -u` command: it bypasses TLS verification, exposes credentials in process/log context and is not SNMP evidence.
Preserve and hash existing SEL/syslog/audit chronology before any separately approved time change; do not clear logs to create a baseline.
For read-only comparison, sample the SNMP object, trusted reference and any approved Redfish source closely enough to account for transit delay and rollover.
For a future SET path, stop on NTP override, time-source disagreement, certificate/authentication failure, scheduled-action impact, log discontinuity or loss of BMC access; no automatic retry.
Do not treat successful Redfish DateTime GET as proof of SNMP object visibility or SNMP write coverage.
agent_execution_scope: Before the decision, perform no clock action and only preserve the review conflict.
After a GET-only decision, securely read the exact SNMPv3 `spClock` object and compare encoding/timezone/delta with a trusted reference; use Redfish only as an approved independent cross-check.

After a separately approved SET decision, a later agent may perform exactly the approved set/readback/impact/restore sequence under engineer observation; this review authorizes neither path by itself.
engineer_actions: Decide and document whether the authoritative purpose is read-only clock validation or writable SNMP configuration.
Approve the OID/encoding/reference/tolerance and secure tool path; for SET, approve value, maintenance window, impact evidence and recovery/restore.
Observe any state-changing execution, validate final time/log/certificate/schedule health and issue PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The proposed Redfish GET is a different interface, assumes a fixed Manager URI, bypasses TLS verification and exposes credentials; it cannot resolve or prove the source's SNMP configure semantics.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: No executable command is valid until engineering selects GET versus SET. Then use the exact vendor SNMPv3 object with protected secrets and trusted reference; any Redfish read remains separate corroboration with CA validation.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: IReasoning, SNMPv3 setup, undefined `$target`, Net-SNMP GET criterion, source `Clear logs` step and 10/5-minute values remain preserved evidence rather than silently rewritten.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Define two non-equivalent checkpoints: SNMPv3 GET accuracy/encoding against a synchronized reference, or explicitly approved SNMPv3 SET followed by readback, impact inspection and restoration. Execute only the selected checkpoint and report untested coverage.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The identified BMC firmware, clock/NTP policy and matching vendor MIB with documented `spClock` access.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC firmware, MIB, SNMP client, NTP/timezone policy and any Redfish service versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor `spClock` MIB definition and BMC time/NTP/event-log/certificate documentation plus Project acceptance.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Exposes the source's hidden read/write fork instead of assuming configuration from the item name or downgrading it to a read.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: GET proves visibility and accuracy only; SET/readback/restore proves configuration behavior. Redfish GET proves neither SNMP transport nor SNMP write semantics.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Engineer purpose decision, object/access/encoding, reference/tolerance and, if writable, impact/recovery contract.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Time mutation can reorder logs, invalidate correlation, interact with NTP, affect certificate/authentication checks and trigger scheduled behavior.

project_override_considerations: A Project may approve a GET-only override, but must record that `configure`/SET coverage remains unverified. A Project may select another approved configuration interface only with original/actual tool, reason, semantic equivalence and unverified SNMP coverage explicitly recorded.
expected_evidence: engineering decision identifying GET-only or SET purpose and resulting coverage
vendor `spClock` OID/type/access/encoding/timezone definition and redacted SNMPv3 setup
trusted reference, synchronized sampling timestamps and delta/tolerance calculation
secure CA-validated Redfish evidence only when approved as a separate cross-check
if SET: pre-change logs/time/NTP/certificate/schedule state, approved value, SET response, readback, impacts, exact restore and final health
tool/coverage statement, no-clear confirmation and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items require `configureSP.spClock`, but Procedure/Criteria contain read-only Get operations and never specify a SET or restore. DeepSeek further substitutes an unsafe Redfish GET while saying monitor/configure. These are different core operations and coverage domains.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The unresolved operation is not merely a missing parameter: GET-only accuracy and SET/readback/restore have materially different purpose, blast radius and acceptance. Neither can be selected without changing or guessing the preserved source intent, so engineering must decide before execution design.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Rejects Redfish GET and TLS bypass as SNMP configuration evidence and rejects inferred SET coverage.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees that BLOCKED is warranted by core operation ambiguity, not by the missing OID/reference alone.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Independently confirms its technical block but corrects the invalid next-row mapping and strengthens source-preserving Project Override coverage rules.

review_improvement: Defines the precise engineer-owned fork, prevents a safe read from being mislabeled as clock configuration, and protects chronological, authentication and scheduled-action evidence before any possible time mutation.
independent_technical_reasoning: A clock GET and SET are not interchangeable. A GET can be bounded and low risk, whereas a SET can change forensic ordering, NTP behavior, certificate validation and scheduled actions and requires restoration. Because the source contradicts itself on that core operation, V3.1's readiness rule does not remove the block.
